newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Government would not hand over financial information about the risk profile of individual municipalities - an estimated one third of which are financially unviable - to the private sector as this would undermine its attempt to monitor their finances, Trevor Manuel and Valli Moosa siad at a briefing on Tuesday.

- Gauteng education would receive five billion rand of the province's 13.718 billion rand budget allocation, an eleven percent increase from last year but a 9.5 percent reduction from current spending levels, finance and economic affairs MEC Jabu Moleketi said in his budget speech on Tuesday.

- The Katz commission has failed to reach a definitive position on wealth taxes, saying that capital transfer taxes, are desirable on some grounds but are impractical to implement and unlikely to produce high returns.

- President Nelson Mandela had asked Inkatha Freedom Party leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi to accompany him on visits to African countries so that they could jointly advocate peace in the strife-torn continent, an IFP source said on Tuesday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Sanlam, the country's second-largest life assurer, said on Tuesday that its year to December 31 1996 had been made difficult by a hefty tax bill and an upsurge in the number of people who stopped paying policies.
- Mr Price, the clothing retailer, launched a scathing attack on the textile and clothing industries this week, accusing them of wanting to put it out of business.
- UAL Merchant Bank, a merchank bank in the Nedcor group, is seeking a foreign partner for a twenty to thirty percent equity stake, Chris Pearce, UAL's managing director, said on Tuesday night.

- The Concerned Medical Scheme Group, a new body representing more than a million members and their dependents, is planning to lobby the health department against proposals to restructure the funding of private healthcare which, it claims "ultimately will increase prices and decrease coverage", said Adrian Gore, the chief executive of Momentum Life.

- A broker at RMB Securities on Tuesday sold about ninety nine million Quickco shares when meaning to deal in just 99,000 shares, a deal which prompted a speculative flurry on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD
- The manner in which South Africans are taxed on capital transfers is apparently not going to be changed much when a new tax system is introduced.
- Almost 43 percent of all new policies that Sanlam sold to individuals last year were surrendered, managing director Desmond Smith said.
- The special fund which government plans to launch to economically empower black people will start functioning in the middle of this year.
THE STAR

- South Africa wanted peace to prevail in the Middle East and had thus decided not to continue with a proposed multibillion-rand order for sophisticated tank sight systems for Syria's main battle tanks, Defence Minister Joe Modise said on Tuesday.

- Incubators and cots in maternity wards in Gauteng hospitals are being filled by healthy babies who have been abandoned and have to languish their because there is no space in the province's overflowing children's homes.

- Kevin (thirteen) has only ever known one home - the paediatric ward of Coronation Hospital in Coronationville, Johannesburg. His bed and minimal possesions occupy a corner of the stark ward. He rarely has a visitor, and social workers and nursing staff are his "family".
- Why does Chelsea, daughter of American President Bill Clinton, always accompany her parents on official state visits.
